text: Abroad. This is my first time abroad.
Orientation. Orientation is on Monday morning.
Roommate. My roommate is from Japan.
Canteen. Everybody eats in the canteen at half past twelve.
Uniform. I have never worn a uniform before.
Timetable. My timetable has six subjects.
Accent. The accent here is faster than on TV.
Sunscreen. Nobody goes out without sunscreen here.
Have you ever been abroad?
I have never worn a uniform.
No, I haven't. Have you?
You are the exchange kid, right? Have you ever been to Australia before?
Never. First time abroad, actually.
No way. And they put you straight into orientation with jet lag?
This morning. I have not slept properly since Tuesday.
Brutal. Have you met your roommate yet?
Yeah, he is from Japan. He has been here for a month already.
Good, he can show you the canteen. Have you ever worn a uniform?
Never in my life. And I have no idea how to read this timetable.
Give it here. And put sunscreen on, mate. You have never seen a sun like this one.
Have you ever been to Australia?
No, I never have. This is my first time.
I have never worn a uniform before.
I have already met my roommate.
Sorry, can you say that again? The accent is fast.

Morning everyone, and welcome. Quick orientation, five minutes, then you are free. First, the timetable. You have six subjects and every one of them is on the sheet in your folder. Second, uniform. Yes, you have to wear it, yes, every day, and no, nobody likes it. Third, the canteen opens at half past twelve and it closes at one fifteen, so do not be late. And the one thing I say to every exchange student who has just arrived: sunscreen. Every day, even when it is cloudy. Half of you have never lived with this sun and it will find you.

So you just got here? Right, I have been here for five weeks, so let me save you some time. I have made every mistake already. I have missed the bus twice, I have turned up to the wrong classroom, and I have gone to the canteen at one twenty, which is closed. Also, I have never seen anybody eat lunch alone here, so just sit down at any table, nobody cares. And do not worry about the accent. I did not understand a word in the first week. Now I understand about eighty per cent, which is enough.
